name: FTP Consumer
helpText: This scheduled consumer uses an FTP message provider and supports absolute or relative schedules.
allowableProperties_comment: Note that the order of properties in this file dictates the order displayed on screen, unless propertyDisplayOrder is set, which will be used as the primary key

componentName.helpText: The name of the component as displayed on diagrams. The name should be unique for the flow. The name will be used internally to reflect the bean created.

active.helpText: Optional only available on FTP consumer. Default: false. Indicates indicating whether the FTP connection is active or passive.

ageOfFiles.helpText: The number of days to retain metadata about processed files for duplicate detection. The default, -1, retains it indefinitely.

checksum.helpText: Default: false. Indicates indicating whether to verify integrity of retrieved file by comparing with a checksum supplied by the remote system.

chronological.helpText: Default: true. If true (the default), when multiple files are available, process the oldest first; if false, order of processing is non-deterministic.

chunkSize.helpText: Size of chunks to use (when chunking=true). Default(1048576) 1MB.

chunking.helpText: If true, file download should be performed in smaller distinguished data chunks of size defined by chunkSize configuration. Default is false.

cleanupJournalOnComplete.helpText: Only set to false when debugging. When true (default) the journal information is deleted when the file is processed successfully. The journal is a durable log of in-progress FTP operations, letting the connector detect and safely replay/resolve transactions interrupted by a crash — instead of losing or duplicating file processing.

clientID.helpText: ClientID is used in the persisted metadata to identify this component uniquely in the context of the module. Since a flow can have only one consumer, the flow name makes for a good, default, client ID.

configuration.helpText: If you don't want to use properties files, you can supply a configuration bean that encapsulates all the properties here which gets bound via Spring @ConfigurationProperties. This might also be useful if you want to extend the configuration with fields the builder doesn't expose. Using it will reduce your ability to configure the component within this tool.
configuration.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the Configuration bean.

configurationId.helpText: By default, the configuration ID is moduleName + flowName + componentName + componentType. Override it when multiple flows should share a configuration, or when renaming a flow without changing configuration already stored in the override-properties database.

connectionTimeout.helpText: Internal (S)FTP connector connection timeout value in milliseconds. Default is 60000 (1 minute).

criticalOnStartup.helpText: Default: false. Identifies this component as being critical for starting the flow i.e. if the component fails to start, the whole flow will not start.

cronExpression.helpText: Cron based expression dictating the invocation schedule for this component. Example, '*/5 * * * * ?' will fire every 5 seconds.

dataTimeout.helpText: Internal FTP connector data connection timeout value in milliseconds. Default is 300000 (5 minutes).

destructive.helpText: Deletes the file after successful consumption. Default is false.

eager.helpText: When true (default is false), attempt to process all available files. MaxEagerCallbacks can be used to limit the number of files before reverting to business schedule.

eventFactory.helpText: Provide the classname that overrides and implements the default EventFactory interface. The Event factory used to instantiate ikasan flow events based on incoming payload from the tech endpoint. Pre-built implementations you can wire in instead of writing your own: org.ikasan.spec.flow.FlowEventFactory (Ikasan's built-in default, used automatically unless overridden).
eventFactory.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the Configuration bean.

filenamePattern.helpText: A full Java regular expression (not a shell glob) matched against candidate filenames on the remote server - e.g. '.*\.csv' matches any CSV file. A shell-style glob like '*.tmp' will fail at runtime with a PatternSyntaxException (a bare '*' has nothing to repeat) - use '.*\.tmp' instead. To match a literal filename, escape any regex-significant characters in it, particularly '.', e.g. 'invoice\.txt' (an unescaped 'invoice.txt' would also match 'invoiceXtxt', since '.' means "any character" in a regex).
filenamePattern.validationMessage: This must be a Java regular expression, not a shell glob - a bare *, + or ? at the very start has nothing to repeat and fails at runtime with a PatternSyntaxException. Did you mean '.*' instead of '*'? e.g. '.*\.txt' matches any .txt file.

filterDuplicates.helpText: When true (the default), duplicate files are ignored based on previously persisted metadata, such as the processing timestamp.

filterOnFilename.helpText: When true (the default), the full remote path (not just the bare filename) is used to determine if this file is a duplicate. Also requires filterDuplicates to be true. Also required filterDuplicates to be true.

filterOnLastModifiedDate.helpText: When true (the default), the last modified date of the file is used to determine if this file is a duplicate. Also requires filterDuplicates to be true.

ftps.helpText: If true, the connection will be made using FTPs (FTP over SSL). Default is false.

ftpsIsImplicit.helpText: Requires FTPS. When false (the default), the client uses explicit FTPS (FTPES, defined by RFC 4217): it connects to the standard FTP port (21 by default), then upgrades the connection with AUTH TLS or AUTH SSL before authentication. When true, it uses deprecated implicit FTPS, starting the TLS/SSL handshake immediately on connection; the default port is 990.

ftpsKeyStoreFilePassword.helpText: The password for the keystore file used to validate the server certificate. Mandatory once ftps is enabled - there is no fallback to a default Java keystore; the connection will fail to establish if this is left blank while ftps is true.

ftpsKeyStoreFilePath.helpText: The path to the keystore file used to validate the server certificate. Mandatory once ftps is enabled - there is no fallback to a default Java keystore; the connection will fail to establish if this is left blank while ftps is true.

ftpsPort.helpText: Requires ftps to be true. Default(21) only applicable when FTPS=true. The remote port of FTPs server where consumer needs to connect.

ftpsProtocol.helpText: Requires ftps to be true. SSL/TLS protocol name used to negotiate the FTPS connection (e.g. "SSL", "TLS", "TLSv1.2"), passed to Java's SSLContext. The Ikasan defaults is "SSL"; "TLS" is the more modern, explicit choice.

ignoreMisfire.helpText: Default: true. When true, ignore Quartz misfires (a missed scheduled cron fire time, e.g. due to scheduler downtime) and simply wait for the next scheduled time; if false, Quartz will fire the job once immediately to catch up on the missed run.

isRecursive.helpText: Default: false. Works together with sourceDirectory and filenamePattern: if true, recurse into subdirectories of sourceDirectory (unlimited depth), and filenamePattern is applied to files found there too, not just files directly in sourceDirectory. Useful when consuming from a top-level directory without knowing its full subdirectory structure.

managedEventIdentifierService.helpText: Optional, and safe to leave unset for most flows. Ikasan gives every message a tracking ID as it processes it - used to correlate a message in the audit trail/dashboard, and to recognise the same message again if a flow error 'parks' it for later retry. By default this ID is just a raw hash of the file's content (functional, but not human-readable). Setting this property lets you supply your own class to derive a more meaningful ID instead - for file consumers, a common choice is org.ikasan.component.endpoint.filetransfer.ManagedEventFileTransferIdentifierService, which uses the filename, making it much easier to recognise in the dashboard.
managedEventIdentifierService.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the consumer event provider bean.

maxEagerCallbacks.helpText: Default(0), meaning unlimited. The maximum number of consecutive eager scheduled callbacks (when eager is set to true) before reverting to business schedule.

maxRows.helpText: When housekeeping the metadata, i.e. ageOfFiles has been exceeded, this will set the batch size for deletion. The default, -1, means unlimited.

messageProvider.helpText: Provide the classname that overrides and implements the default MessageProvider interface. The message provider is responsible for providing the message payload. Pre-built implementations you can wire in instead of writing your own: org.ikasan.component.endpoint.quartz.consumer.QuartzMessageProvider, org.ikasan.component.endpoint.quartz.consumer.CallBackMessageProvider, org.ikasan.component.endpoint.filesystem.messageprovider.FileMessageProvider, org.ikasan.component.endpoint.filesystem.messageprovider.CorrelatingFileMessageProvider, org.ikasan.component.endpoint.db.messageprovider.DbMessageProvider, org.ikasan.endpoint.sftp.consumer.SftpMessageProvider, org.ikasan.endpoint.ftp.consumer.FtpMessageProvider.
messageProvider.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the Message Provider bean.

minAge.helpText: The minimum age of the file on the remote filesystem before file can be processed. This setting is in place to prevent (S)FTP consumer from picking up file which is still being written to. The default is 120 seconds.

moveOnSuccess.helpText: Default: false. Indicates indicating whether to move the processed file after successful consumption to different location defined by moveOnSuccessNewPath configuration.

moveOnSuccessNewPath.helpText: Optional only applicable when moveOnSuccess is set to true, it provides new directory path for the processed file to be moved to.

password.helpText: Password used to login to (S)FTP server where consumer needs to connect. Takes precedences over privateKeyFilename. If both provided user/password combination will be used to login rather then user/privateKeyFilename.

passwordFilePath.helpText: The path of the file that contains the password.

remoteHost.helpText: Default('127.0.0.1') host name of the remote (S)FTP server where consumer needs to connect.

remotePort.helpText: Default(21) port of the remote (S)FTP server where consumer needs to connect.

renameOnSuccess.helpText: Default: false. Indicates indicating whether to rename the processed file after successful consumption.

renameOnSuccessExtension.helpText: Requires renameOnSuccess to be true (in which case this MUST be set). This is the extension appended to the file on the remote system after successful processing, e.g. '.processed'. May include an embedded timestamp using /[dateFormat]/, e.g. '/yyyyMMddHHmmss/.complete'.

socketTimeout.helpText: Internal FTP connector socket connection timeout value. Default is 300000 milliseconds.

sourceDirectory.helpText: Remote directory from which to discover files, e.g. /home/myuser/inbound. Whether this path resolves relative to the account's home directory or the server's real filesystem root depends entirely on the FTP server's configuration (e.g. vsftpd chroot_local_user) - confirm with the server admin, or use the full absolute path if unsure. A wrong value here causes the consumer to silently find zero files, with no error logged.

sourceDirectoryURLFactory.helpText: Provide the classname that overrides and implements the DirectoryURLFactory interface. The factory provides more flexible way of defining source directory. Most common use case would be when source directory changes names for instance based on date.
sourceDirectoryURLFactory.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the Source Directory URL Factory bean.

systemKey.helpText: Optional. Overrides FTP server-type auto-detection for parsing directory listings — normally the client infers this from the server's SYST reply, but that can be unreliable. Set to one of Apache Commons Net's FTPClientConfig system keys if listings come back empty or malformed, e.g. 'UNIX', 'WINDOWS', 'OS/400', 'VMS', 'AS/400'.

timezone.helpText: Optional. The timezone the cronExpression schedule is evaluated in, e.g. 'America/New_York' or 'Europe/London'. If left unset, the JVM's own default timezone is used — only set this if the schedule needs to run consistently in a specific timezone regardless of where the module is deployed.

transactionManager.helpText: Provide the classname that overrides and implements the default JtaTransactionManager interface. Typically this is the Spring transaction manager, overriding may be needed to interface into third party containers.
transactionManager.validationMessage: Provide a java classname for the transaction manager bean.

username.helpText: User name used to login to (S)FTP server where consumer needs to connect.
